title: Finite common-stage Hom lifting and eventual equality
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$ and an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-pur-conventions]. Let $X,X_i$ be finite-type $k$-schemes, $j_i:X_i\to X$ morphisms [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and $I$ a finite set, possibly empty. Use the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], raw rational categories [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and common-stage pair categories [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Write $r_{E,i}=Lj_i^*$ for the rational derived pullback of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], with the rationalized canonical scalar comparisons $b^i_{L/E,K}:r_{E,i}K\otimes_EL\xrightarrow{\sim}r_{L,i}(K\otimes_EL)$ of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension], with their identity and tower compatibilities [lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition]. Assume $R_E=(r_{E,i})_i$ is fully faithful at every finite coefficient field $E\subset\Omega$ [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set].

For global pair objects $A=(E,K)$ and $B=(F,M)$, common-stage restriction, whose component representative of $[L,u]$ is
$$[L,(b^i_{L/F,M})^{-1}\circ r_{L,i}(u)\circ b^i_{L/E,K}],$$
induces a bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}(A,B)\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}((E,r_{E,i}K),(F,r_{F,i}M)).$$
Every tuple on the right has a simultaneous representative and a preimage $u:K\otimes_EL\to M\otimes_FL$ at a single finite $L\supset E,F$, which can also contain any prescribed finite list of coefficient fields. More precisely, for component representatives $v_i$ at $L_i\supset E,F$ one can choose any common finite upper field $L\supset L_i,E,F$, transport every $v_i$ there using the scalar-tower isomorphisms, and choose $u$ with
$$r_{L,i}(u)=b^i_{L/F,M}\circ(v_i)_L\circ(b^i_{L/E,K})^{-1}.$$
For representatives $u_0,u_1$ of two global arrows at fields $L_0,L_1$, their component classes are equal for every $i$ if and only if the transported global representatives agree over some finite $N\supset L_0,L_1$. Given component equality witnesses at finitely many fields, $N$ can be any common upper field also containing the representatives' fields. No injectivity of transition maps on Hom groups is required. For $I=\varnothing$ the Hom set is a singleton, and the common field for the empty family can be $\mathbf Q_\ell$ enlarged to contain the fields of the endpoints and representatives.

proof.text: Use the unique coherent pullback stage-system morphism supplied by lem-sf-rational-direct-image-coefficient-compatibility. Its functor family is the literal rationalDerivedPullback and its beta components are commonStagePullbackComparison. Substitute these components in StageSystem.Morphism.tr_mapAt to prove stageRestriction commutes with transport. No right-adjoint mate assertion is used.

The chosen common-stage pullback functor satisfies its representative formula by commonStageDerivedPullback_existsUnique. Conjugation by its specified object equalities converts the heterogeneous formula to restrictionHom_ofHom.

Induct over any finite list of coefficient fields. Start with the compositum of the endpoint fields (also for the empty list); at insertion replace the upper field by its compositum with the new field. The finite-coefficient compositum bounds preserve all earlier lower bounds. Every component Hom class has a representative, so this supplies one common upper field for all component representatives and any prescribed finite list. At this field, conjugate the transported representatives by inverse source comparison and target comparison. Stagewise surjectivity supplies a global stage arrow. Cancelling the comparisons proves the restriction formula and therefore simultaneous lifting and surjectivity. The same stagewise surjectivity proves the displayed lifting assertion at any given upper field.

For two representatives, assume component transport equality at witness fields Ni. Transport each equality to any N containing every Ni and the original representative fields. StageSystem.tr_tr and the transport compatibility from step 1 identify the resulting equalities with equality of the restrictions of the two global transports. Cancel both endpoint comparisons and use stagewise injectivity to equate these global transports. For equality of component classes, the representatives theorem supplies the actual Ni. Take a finite compositum of them and both original fields. Eventual equality then proves equality of global classes, giving injectivity. Conversely applying restrictionHom to equal global classes gives equal components. Combine this injectivity with the representatives equality criterion to obtain the eventual-equality iff.

Combine injectivity and surjectivity to obtain bijectivity. If I is empty, its unique empty tuple has a preimage by surjectivity, giving Nonempty Hom. For any two arrows their component functions agree by elimination from I, and injectivity equates them. This gives Subsingleton Hom without requiring I to be nonempty or any Hom transition to be injective.
